cli-help.title: bowerloom --help
cli-help.caption: The short help lists the commands you use first.

lines.text: Setup does not start workers, grant runtime access, or authorize connected actions.
Set up agent teams, skills, and prompts for Claude Code and Codex.
bowerloom up --team <name>                   Prepare this project for a team. Shows each plan first.
bowerloom ls [teams|skills|prompts|slices]   List what this project holds.
bowerloom status                             Show whether this project is ready.
bowerloom help context                       Give each agent its part of a knowledge base.
bowerloom skills check                       Check the pins in .bowerloom/skills.json.
bowerloom skills sync [--offline]            Install the pinned skills on this machine.
Every change shows a plan first. Agents pass --approve <revision> or --json.
No command here starts workers yet.
bowerloom help store       Your store, ~/.bowerloom, and how a project uses it.

cli-up.title: bowerloom up
cli-up.caption: Up prints a plan and a revision, and writes nothing until you approve.

lines.text: bowerloom up --team first --goal "Write the weekly report"
Next step: init. Set up .bowerloom in this folder for team first.
Folder: ~/projects/sample (an existing folder: adds .bowerloom only, and your files stay as they are)
Creates 20 setup files and a private installation receipt in .bowerloom.
Then each run shows the next step, if any: team, skills sync and apply, each with its own plan. Workers stay held.
This writes setup files only. It starts no workers and runs nothing.
Approval required. Run the same command again with --approve <revision>

cli-ls.caption: The list shows the teams, skills, prompts, and slices of the project.

This writes inside .bowerloom only. It starts no workers and runs nothing.

lines.text: Workers: none started (this beta starts none)

cli-init-plan.title: bowerloom init plan
cli-init-plan.caption: The plan lists the files before any is written.

lines.text: bowerloom init plan --mode new --target ~/projects/new-project --name "Sample team" --goal "Review a synthetic team setup" --profile engineer
Goal: Review a synthetic team setup
Your existing personal agent remains your interface.
Proposed team: Engineering lead → Implementation maker → Code reviewer
Engineering lead: Defines the implementation scope and checks. Proposed write: output/scope.md (proposed local write; separate action approval)
Implementation maker: Drafts the change proposal and failure cases. Proposed write: output/draft.md (proposed local write; separate action approval)
Code reviewer: Checks correctness, security, and test evidence. Proposed write: output/review.md (proposed local write; separate action approval)
Access: supplied brief assets and accepted task outputs only. No context or settings imported.
Limits: at most 2 active workers; 25% capacity reserve; no paid fallback.
Installation identity: the reviewed Darwin policy accepts the saved birth time or its one directional floating-point conversion. Device, inode, owner, mode, paths and managed bytes must still match.
Project-root metadata changes can still invalidate existing enrollment and links. Active changes and recovery ownership stay exact.
Installation approval: create only the reviewed .bowerloom files. No workers, backend, network, or project execution.
Proposed task permissions are not granted by this approval. All future task writes require separate exact approval.
Creates 20 setup files and a private installation receipt in .bowerloom. Keep the receipt out of shared definitions.
Read startup-review.md for roles, access, limits, and expandable technical contents. Review setup text for private information before sharing.
For every file, content hash, and compiler detail, rerun this plan with --json before approval.
Review first. Apply with unchanged inputs and --approve followed by this exact revision.
Setup is ready for review. No team has started and no execution permission was granted.

cli-apply.title: bowerloom apply
cli-apply.caption: Apply prints a plan of the copies it will put in place.

lines.text: Apply skills, prompts, and agents for Claude Code and Codex, and context slices for Claude Code
Network: none. Apply never fetches. A pin that is not cached yet needs bowerloom skills sync first.
Copies go to .bowerloom/managed, .claude and .agents, and stay on this machine. Apply adds copies and removes none.
This copies text files only. It starts no workers and runs nothing.
Bowerloom never edits AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md. To point your agents at these copies, add a line like this to AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md yourself:

Project skills are in .claude/skills and .agents/skills. Prompts are Claude Code commands in .claude/commands, and Codex skills named prompt-<name>. Agents are in .claude/agents. Context slices are skills named slice-<name> in .claude/skills.
Approval required. Run the same command again with --approve <revision>
